pages.title: Commercial Pool
pages.description: A public or semi-public pool subject to health department regulations and inspection.

pages.title: Concrete Pool
pages.description: A plastered or pebbled concrete pool requiring higher calcium hardness (200–400 ppm).

pages.title: Copper
pages.description: A metal that can enter pool water from ionizers, algaecides, or corroded equipment, causing green staining.

pages.title: Corrosion
pages.description: Damage to pool surfaces and metal equipment caused by corrosive (low LSI) water.

pages.title: Pool Cover
pages.description: A cover that reduces evaporation, heat loss, debris entry, and UV degradation of chemicals.

pages.title: Cyanuric Acid
pages.description: A chemical stabilizer that protects chlorine from UV degradation in outdoor pools.

pages.title: DE Filter
pages.description: A diatomaceous earth filter offering the finest filtration (3–5 microns) of any pool filter type.

pages.title: Emergency Recovery Reference
pages.description: A printable quick-reference for emergency pool and spa recovery scenarios.

pages.title: EPA
pages.description: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency — regulates disinfectants including pool chemicals.

pages.title: Eye Irritation
pages.description: Swimmer eye irritation caused by chloramines or pH imbalance.

pages.title: Fiberglass Pool
pages.description: A pre-molded pool with a smooth fiberglass surface requiring moderate calcium levels.

pages.title: Filtration
pages.description: The continuous mechanical removal of suspended particles from pool water.

pages.title: Flow Rate
pages.description: The volume of water the pump moves per minute — a key factor in turnover rate.

pages.title: Foaming
pages.description: Persistent foam on pool or spa water surface caused by surfactants, high TDS, or algaecide.

pages.title: Free Chlorine
pages.description: The active, unsaturated chlorine available to sanitize pool water.

pages.title: Gallons
pages.description: US liquid gallon — the standard unit of pool volume measurement.

pages.title: Green Water
pages.description: Pool water discolored green by algae bloom due to insufficient free chlorine.

pages.title: Pool Heater
pages.description: A device that raises water temperature using gas, electric heat pump, or solar energy.

pages.title: High Chlorine
pages.description: Free chlorine above 5 ppm causing bleaching, eye/skin irritation, and swimmer discomfort.

pages.title: High pH
pages.description: Pool water pH above 7.8, reducing chlorine effectiveness and promoting scale formation.

pages.title: Hot Tub
pages.description: A small, heated pool (75–500 gallons) used for relaxation and hydrotherapy.

pages.title: Hydrogen Peroxide
pages.description: An oxidizer used in non-chlorine pool systems and as an emergency chlorine neutralizer.

pages.title: Indoor Pool
pages.description: A pool housed inside a building, requiring ventilation management and no CYA.

pages.title: Iron
pages.description: A metal dissolved in pool water that causes rust-brown staining when oxidized.

pages.title: LaMotte
pages.description: LaMotte Company — manufacturer of professional water testing equipment for pool and spa use.

pages.title: Liquid Chlorine
pages.description: Sodium hypochlorite solution (10–12.5%) — the most commonly used liquid pool sanitizer.

pages.title: Liters
pages.description: SI unit of volume — 1 US gallon equals approximately 3.785 liters.

pages.title: Low Chlorine
pages.description: Free chlorine below the minimum effective level for the current CYA concentration.

pages.title: Low pH
pages.description: Pool water pH below 7.2, causing corrosion, eye irritation, and equipment damage.

pages.title: Langelier Saturation Index
pages.description: A composite score indicating whether water is balanced, corrosive, or scale-forming.

pages.title: Pool Maintenance Checklist
pages.description: A printable weekly pool maintenance checklist covering testing, cleaning, and chemical additions.

pages.title: Hot Tub Maintenance Log
pages.description: A printable log for recording hot tub and spa water tests, chemical additions, and service notes.

pages.title: Manganese
pages.description: A dissolved metal that causes black or purple staining in pool water.

pages.title: Muriatic Acid
pages.description: Hydrochloric acid (31.45%) used to lower pH and total alkalinity in pool water.

pages.title: NSF International
pages.description: NSF International — certifies pool and spa equipment and chemicals to safety standards.

pages.title: Pool Opening Checklist
pages.description: A printable step-by-step checklist for spring pool opening.

pages.title: ORP
pages.description: Oxidation-Reduction Potential — an electrical measurement of water's sanitizing capacity.

pages.title: Outdoor Pool
pages.description: A pool exposed to direct sunlight and weather, requiring CYA stabilization of chlorine.

pages.title: Oxidation
pages.description: The chemical destruction of organic compounds, combined chlorine, and contaminants in pool water.

pages.title: Ozone
pages.description: A powerful oxidizer generated on-site and injected into pool water as a supplemental sanitizer.

pages.title: pH
pages.description: The measure of hydrogen ion concentration indicating acidity or alkalinity of pool water.

pages.title: Phosphate
pages.description: A nutrient compound in pool water that can fuel algae growth.

pages.title: PHTA
pages.description: Pool & Hot Tub Alliance — the primary industry trade association for pool and spa professionals.

pages.title: Pool Opening
pages.description: The spring start-up process to prepare a pool for the swimming season.

pages.title: Pool Salt
pages.description: High-purity sodium chloride (99.8%+) for use in saltwater pool systems.

pages.title: Parts Per Million
pages.description: The standard unit for measuring chemical concentrations in pool water.

pages.title: Pool Pump
pages.description: The motor and impeller assembly that circulates water through the filtration and chemical treatment system.

pages.title: Salt
pages.description: Sodium chloride dissolved in pool water to enable chlorine generation by a salt chlorinator.

pages.title: Salt Chlorinator
pages.description: An electrolytic cell that converts dissolved salt into hypochlorous acid to sanitize pool water.

pages.title: Saltwater Pool
pages.description: A pool that uses a salt chlorinator to generate chlorine on-site from dissolved sodium chloride.

pages.title: Sand Filter
pages.description: A filter using silica sand to trap particles down to 20–40 microns.

pages.title: Sanitizing
pages.description: Maintaining an adequate residual disinfectant to destroy pathogens in pool water.

pages.title: Scaling
pages.description: White or grey mineral deposits on pool surfaces and equipment caused by over-saturated water.

pages.title: Shock Treatment
pages.description: Adding a large dose of chlorine or non-chlorine oxidizer to destroy combined chlorine, algae, and contaminants.

pages.title: Skimmer
pages.description: A wall-mounted intake that removes floating debris from the pool surface before it sinks.

pages.title: Skin Irritation
pages.description: Swimmer skin irritation caused by pH imbalance, chloramines, or high disinfectant levels.

pages.title: Soda Ash
pages.description: Sodium carbonate — used to raise pH in pool water.

pages.title: Dichlor
pages.description: A stabilized granular shock (56–62% available chlorine) that adds both chlorine and CYA.

pages.title: Stabilizer / CYA Granules
pages.description: Granular cyanuric acid product used to raise CYA to the target stabilizer level.

pages.title: Strong Chlorine Smell
pages.description: A pungent chlorine odor caused by chloramines, not excess chlorine.

pages.title: Swim Spa
pages.description: A larger spa (12–20 ft) with jets for swimming in place and hydrotherapy.

pages.title: Swimming Pool
pages.description: A permanent or above-ground body of water designed for recreational swimming.

pages.title: Taylor Technologies
pages.description: Taylor Technologies — manufacturer of professional pool test kits and the standard reference for pool chemistry calculations.

pages.title: Temperature
pages.description: Water temperature in °F or °C, affecting chemical reactions, chlorine demand, and comfort.

pages.title: Water Testing
pages.description: Measuring pool water chemistry parameters using test strips, liquid kits, or digital testers.

pages.title: Total Chlorine
pages.description: The sum of free chlorine and combined chlorine in pool water.

pages.title: Total Dissolved Solids
pages.description: The cumulative concentration of all dissolved matter in pool water.

pages.title: Trichlor Tablets
pages.description: Stabilized chlorine tablets (90% available chlorine) for use in automatic chlorinators and floaters.

pages.title: Turnover Time
pages.description: The time required for the pump to circulate the entire pool volume through the filter once.

pages.title: °C
pages.description: Degrees Celsius — the SI temperature unit used in metric countries.

pages.title: Days
pages.description: Unit of time — used for maintenance scheduling and chemical activity timelines.

pages.title: °F
pages.description: Degrees Fahrenheit — the standard temperature unit for pool and spa temperature in North America.

pages.title: US Gallons
pages.description: US liquid gallon — the primary volume unit for pool calculations in North America.

pages.title: Hours
pages.description: Unit of time — used for turnover rate and pump run time calculations.

pages.title: Metric Liters
pages.description: 1 liter = 0.2642 US gallons = 1,000 milliliters. Used in metric countries for pool volume measurement. Chemical concentrations in mg/L are equivalent to ppm.

pages.title: mg/L
pages.description: Milligrams per liter — numerically identical to ppm in aqueous solutions.

pages.title: Minutes
pages.description: Unit of time — used for pump turnover calculation and wait times after chemical additions.

pages.title: Months
pages.description: Unit of time — used for seasonal maintenance intervals and hot tub water change schedules.

pages.title: ppm
pages.description: Parts per million — the standard concentration unit for pool chemistry.

pages.title: Weeks
pages.description: Unit of time — used for maintenance scheduling (weekly testing, weekly shock).

pages.title: Vinyl Pool
pages.description: A pool with a vinyl liner surface requiring lower calcium hardness targets.

pages.title: Water Replacement
pages.description: Partially or completely draining and refilling pool or spa water to reduce dissolved compound levels.

pages.title: Water Test Log
pages.description: A printable log for recording water test results over time to track chemistry trends.

pages.title: Winterization
pages.description: The process of closing a pool or hot tub for the winter to prevent freeze damage.
